messages:
elaine: Quick sync — I just opened a PR that changes empty-prompt handling in the runtime. It alters token outputs for edge cases. Is this a patch or minor?
sam: personally i'd call that a minor since behaviour changed. Even if API surface same, semantics changed and downstream could rely on old tokens.
anya: hmm. We normally reserve minor for user-facing API changes. This is internal, but I agree it could break customers. Could we ship as patch + opt-in flag?
mike: opt-in flag is doable but adds churn. Another option: release as patch but add explicit release-note + recommend pinning to exact patch until app owners validate.
jess: tagging policy question — do we tag hotfixes as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-hotfix.N` or create `vMAJOR.MINOR.(PATCH+1)`? Our CI picks highest semver, so preferring real patch bumps is simpler.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment job queued: repo=runtime, branch=hotfix/empty-prompt, target=staging, tag=v1.12.4-hotfix. Triggered by @elaine.
elaine: thanks deploy-bot. If we go hotfix tag, we must ensure Dedicated customers pin to `v1.12.3` if they need old behaviour. We should add note to the Dedicated rollout docs.
sam: can we adopt a convention: use plain semver for GA releases (no suffix) and `-hotfix.N` for emergency fixes. Then after validation we cut the next plain patch release `v1.12.4`. That way hotfix tags don't confuse automated deploys but are traceable.
anya: I like that. Also add `changelog/important` label on the PR so release automation picks it for release-notes.
mike: operationally, for Dedicated we should also ship a migration notice and automatic pin suggestion in console: "You're pinned to v1.12.3 — to update to the hotfix, opt in". Ops, please coordinate.
jess: rollback plan: if regressions appear in Canary within 30m, rollback by tagging `v1.12.3-rollback` and invoking `./scripts/rollout --tag=v1.12.3`. We should make rollback CLI idempotent.
sam: add tests to the PR that assert both old and new behaviour guarded under a feature flag so we can flip quickly.
elaine: agreed. Action items: 1) I'll add opt-in flag and update PR, 2) jess can add `-hotfix.N` tagging step to our release script, 3) mike/ops will prepare console pin message for Dedicated.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Staging deploy started: tag=v1.12.4-hotfix, job=5743, started_by=@elaine
anya: FYI change window — let's keep prod deploy to 22:00 UTC to avoid peak for EU customers. If Canary looks clean by 21:30 we'll proceed.
mike: noted. I'll watch Canary and post back — if anything odd i'll trigger rollback and ping #incidents.
jess: will update release-scripts repo with example:
```
# create hotfix tag
git tag -a v1.12.4-hotfix -m "hotfix: empty prompt behavior"
git push origin v1.12.4-hotfix
```
and later for GA patch: `git tag v1.12.4 && git push origin v1.12.4`
sam: tiny nit — ensure our release notes make clear what changed, include input/output samples. Customers who pin can decide.
elaine: will draft release-notes entry and post here once done. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Staging deploy succeeded: job=5743, tag=v1.12.4-hotfix, duration=4m.
mike: Canary looks green after 35m. proceeding with prod at 22:00 UTC unless I hear otherwise.
jess: I've pushed the small script change; also added `--force-rollback` safety check disabled by default.
elaine: release-notes draft: "runtime: fixed empty-prompt handling — changed tokenization for zero-length prompts; opt-in flag available — recommended to pin to v1.12.3 until validated." Posting to docs/announcements after prod.
sam: ok great. Minor vs patch debate settled as hotfix→patch flow. Documented policy note: hotfix tags allowed for emergency, GA patch afterwards.
anya: closing loop — can we add a line in RELEASE_PROCESS.md about this convention? I'll add a PR.
elaine: perfect. closing this thread once prod is live.
